channel.title: IndieHOT — Indie Game Hot Topics
channel.description: IndieHOT collects indie game news from a set of public sources every day and scores it by rules: engines & tools, publishing & marketing, devlogs, industry & funding, events, reviews & postmortems. Only titles, one-line self-written summaries and outbound links are shown — no full text is republished.

item.title: This Tool Brings 2D Painting Workflows Into Unreal Engine 5
item.description: Inky recreates traditional painting materials inside Unreal Engine 5, letting artists paint 3D assets with a 2D workflow.

item.title: Is your data telling you the whole story?
item.description: Fragmented data hides the full player picture — this post explains what it costs UA and monetization teams and how to connect MMP, GA and IAP signals to Unity Vector.

item.title: Sensor Tower introduces web store revenue estimates
item.description: Sensor Tower now estimates direct-to-consumer web store revenue, giving developers a fuller picture of app and game monetisation beyond the stores.

item.title: Hydrilla tutorial: your first BlueFox prop, from prompt to engine
item.description: A step-by-step walkthrough of generating a background prop with Hydrilla's BlueFox 1 from a prompt or reference image, complete with segmented mesh, UVs and PBR maps, while spending generation credits wisely.

item.title: Mesh Topology for Game Assets: A Pre-Export Review Workflow
item.description: A model can look fine in a still render yet pinch at joints or shade oddly in-engine, so the author lays out a pre-export topology review ordered by what each asset has to do.

item.title: Defold Newsletter November 2026
item.description: This month's Defold newsletter rounds up upcoming jams and events, a complete open-source 3D web game sample, and the latest on Xbox support and new assets.

item.title: October 2026 mobile game charts: Top Lords takes off, Tencent falls 11% and AI listens in
item.description: AppMagic's October charts show Top Lords taking off, Tencent down 11%, and AI listening in as the month's big talking points.

item.title: Learn the Art of Making AAA Game-Ready Characters Using Industry-Standard Tools
item.description: This Wingfox master class walks through the complete workflow of creating game-ready characters, aimed at artists who want to reach AAA quality.

item.title: How Unimora is inspiring the next generation of aged care professionals through VR, built with Unity
item.description: Students experience both sides of aged care in VR; Unimora, built with Unity, earned a Unity for Humanity 2026 Honourable Mention.

item.title: Dev snapshot: Godot 4.8 beta 5
item.description: Within a week of beta 4, the Godot team has fixed every remaining launch-blocking issue and is putting out one final snapshot before the release candidate, so developers can try this build and help catch the last bugs before the official release.

item.title: Solitaire with 3D card physics in Rust and WebGL 2, no game engine
item.description: 23 browser card and board games written in about 12,400 lines of Rust, compiled to a single 1.16 MB Wasm file with 3D card physics — no game engine, no physics engine.

item.title: Building a Zero-Dependency Branching Interactive Fiction Engine in 90 Lines of ESM
item.description: A hands-on tutorial building a branching interactive-fiction state machine — conditional choices, relationship meters and a memory ledger — in just 90 lines of dependency-free ESM, with a complete MIT-licensed example project.

item.title: Building a Game-Based Learning Module for UK Schools: A Pre-Production Checklist
item.description: A learning game for UK schools succeeds or fails on decisions made before anyone opens an engine, and this pre-production checklist helps small teams sort out lesson length, shared devices, curriculum fit and data compliance first.

item.title: I built a local Gaussian splat to game-mesh converter, and sold it as a one-off instead of a subscription
item.description: The author turns Gaussian splat scans into game-ready meshes with textures, a collider and two LODs, and shares why they sold the local tool as a one-off instead of a subscription.

item.title: Over 25 Unreal Engine games nominated at The Game Awards 2026
item.description: From Phantom Blade Zero to Meccha Chameleon, a look at the 25-plus Unreal Engine games nominated at The Game Awards 2026.

item.title: Solo Dev Uses AI to Build an Earth-Sized Planet-Scale World
item.description: A veteran developer with 10 years of experience built an Earth-sized planet-scale world with AI, and the demo footage has stunned fellow developers.

item.title: Devs' Frustration: Big Studios Use AI Freely, but Indie Games Get Called Trash for It?
item.description: When big studios use AI it's efficiency, but when indie games do it they're branded trash — this piece looks at the double standard behind that gap.

item.title: The "Cat Game Specialists" Enter China: Douyin and WeChat Mini-Games Bring in Over ¥50M a Month
item.description: An overseas studio known for cat games broke into China's mini-game market and now earns over ¥50 million a month on Douyin and WeChat — a look at how it did it.

item.title: GTA 6 Made $3.79 Billion on Day One: Over Half of Console Players Bought In, Downloads Took 24% of US Bandwidth
item.description: GTA 6 pulled in $3.79 billion on its first day, with over half of console players buying in at launch and downloads at one point taking a quarter of all US bandwidth.

item.title: V.E.T.O.R — A Ruptura: Architecture of an HTML5 Canvas Action-RPG & Limbo Spider Boss Fight (Demo V6.2 Available)
item.description: This indie sci-fi action-RPG skips off-the-shelf engines for a custom dual-layer HTML5 Canvas pipeline synced with video playback — the post breaks down the engine architecture and the Limbo Spider boss fight, with Demo V6.2 available now.
